name: Everything in one sentence (Thursday at 2)
scripted_utterance_templates: I need an initial consultation {day_4_name} at 2.
brief_template: You need an initial consultation by video at exactly 2 PM on {day_4_label}. Your opening line already gave the service, day, and time in one sentence. Accept only that appointment if the scheduler accurately restates it. For the default Sunday-start fixture, the exact line is: I need an initial consultation Thursday at 2.

name: Ambiguous contract matter requires service clarification
brief: You are a new client asking for advice before signing a contract; there is no active dispute and you have never met this lawyer. Do not volunteer those facts until the scheduler clarifies whether you need a general initial consultation or a contract-dispute consultation. Once asked, explain briefly and book a valid initial consultation.

name: Flexible 30-minute follow-up call
scripted_utterance_templates: I need a follow-up call, and I'm flexible this week.
brief: You are an existing client who needs a follow-up call. Any genuinely available day and time works. Accept the first concrete 30-minute phone opening that is offered.

name: 120-minute dispute cannot fit requested day
scripted_utterance_templates: I need a contract dispute consultation on {day_2_name}, around 10.
brief_template: You need the full contract-dispute consultation and initially ask for {day_2_label}, whose fragmented windows cannot hold 120 minutes. Never accept a shortened appointment. If the scheduler explains the constraint, you may move to a valid 120-minute opening on {day_3_name}; otherwise politely end without a booking.

name: Decline scripted confirmation, then rebook another day
scripted_utterance_templates: I need an initial consultation {day_4_name} afternoon.
confirmation_response_templates: No, don't book that. I need {day_5_name} instead.
brief_template: You need an initial consultation. Start with {day_4_name} afternoon, but at the first explicit 'shall I book it?' question decline and switch to {day_5_label}. At the next confirmation, affirm only if the proposed appointment is on {day_5_name} and valid.

name: First commit conflicts, re-offer books elsewhere
scripted_utterance_templates: I need a contract dispute consultation {day_4_name} at 2.
brief_template: You need a contract-dispute consultation and initially prefer 2 PM on {day_4_label}. Confirm that first proposal. If told the slot was just taken, accept a different valid 120-minute opening, then explicitly confirm the re-offer.

name: Deterministic human escape
scripted_utterance_templates: Could I speak with a human operator?
brief: Ask for a human operator immediately and do not discuss appointment details.

name: Impossible 120-minute ask stays not booked
scripted_utterance_templates: I need a contract dispute consultation on {day_1_name}, and no other day works.
brief_template: You need the full 120-minute contract-dispute consultation, but the fully blocked {day_1_label} is absolutely the only day you can attend. Refuse every alternate date and every shorter service. Do not affirm any confirmation for another day; remain polite until the scheduler ends the attempt.

name: Early yes cannot bypass the scripted confirm gate
brief: Your second utterance is an ambiguous early yes while the appointment is still being figured out. After that, explain that you are an existing client seeking a flexible follow-up call. Accept a valid time, but commit only after the scheduler asks the explicit scripted 'shall I book it?' question.
